newsitem.title: USA: Memtec rally signals doubt on Gelman deal - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Memtec rally signals doubt on Gelman deal - analysts.

text.p: A rally in the American depository shares of Memtec Ltd indicates doubt on Wall Street about the Australian company's $280-million bid to buy Gelman Sciences, analysts and arbitragers said.
The ADSs of Australia's Memtec were up 3-5/8 to 30-5/8.
The rally may mean arbitragers are skeptical about the Memtec-Gelman deal, said Morgan Stanley analyst Mark Gulley.

An arbitrager who asked not to be named said, "The increase this morning could be a combination of Memtec just returning to its pre-offer price or it could be guys who set up the deal covering their shorts."
The rally started early Thursday after Memtec said it had been advised by Gelman that Gelman received an inquiry about a possible acquisition from Pall Corp.
East Hills, N.Y.-based Pall said later it was engaged in exploratory discussions with Gelman, but has made no offer. All three companies are in the filtration business.
Memtec and Gelman announced a definitive merger agreement on August 30. A spokesman for Memtec's U.S. unit told Reuters Thursday morning the company plans to proceed with the deal.
Shares in Pall were up 1/8 to 26-3/4. Shares in Ann Arbor, Mich.-based Gelman were halted for an imbalance on the American Stock Exchange at 26.
